Against probes that detect harmfulness with ~90%+ recall, attacks drive recall from 100% to 0% while keeping ~90% jailbreak rate; attacks transfer across monitor types (e.g. optimizing against an OOD detector also fools probes). Demonstrates obfuscated activations are abundant in latent space and that defenders cannot guard against all of them even after 70+ rounds of adversarial monitor retraining; also analyzes failures of Circuit Breakers and LAT. Limit: obfuscation degrades performance on complex tasks (SQL).

title: Model Tampering Attacks Enable More Rigorous Evaluations of LLM Capabilities
org: University of Maryland / MIT CSAIL / UK AI Security Institute / Apollo Research
abstract: Argues input-output (input-space) risk evaluations only lower-bound a model's worst-case behavior and cannot assess open-weight risks. Proposes complementing them with model-tampering attacks (latent-activation perturbation and weight fine-tuning). Benchmarks 8 unlearning methods and 9 safety-tuned LLMs against 5 input-space and 6 tampering attacks on WMDP-Bio. Findings: (1) model robustness to capability elicitation lies on a low-dimensional subspace (3 PCs explain 89%); (2) tampering-attack success empirically predicts and conservatively over-estimates held-out input-space attack success (incl. UK AISI proprietary attacks); (3) state-of-the-art unlearning (RMU, RR, ELM, etc.) can be reversed within ~16 fine-tuning steps. No method is robust to all attacks.

title: Neither Valid nor Reliable? Investigating the Use of LLMs as Judges
org: McGill University / Mila - Quebec AI Institute / Statistics Canada
abstract: A position paper arguing that enthusiasm for LLMs-as-judges (LLJs) has outpaced rigorous scrutiny of their validity and reliability. Drawing on measurement theory (construct validity/reliability, Adcock & Collier; Jacobs & Wallach), it critically assesses four core assumptions: LLJs as (1) proxies for human judgment, (2) capable evaluators, (3) scalable evaluators, (4) cost-effective evaluators. It maps documented failures to validity dimensions: convergent validity undermined by inconsistent human-judgment collection; face/discriminant validity threatened by unfaithful explanations, position/verbosity bias, and superficial cues; predictive validity threatened by data contamination, competitive-benchmark gaming, self-enhancement/preference leakage. Grounds analysis in summarization, data annotation, and safety alignment (LLM safety judges misclassify up to 100% of harmful generations as harmless under small perturbations).

title: Jailbreak Distillation: Renewable Safety Benchmarking
org: Microsoft Responsible AI Research / Johns Hopkins University
abstract: Proposes JBDistill, a benchmark-construction framework that 'distills' existing jailbreak attacks into high-quality, easily-updatable safety benchmarks, addressing the comparability/reproducibility gaps of dynamic red-teaming and the saturation/contamination gaps of static benchmarks. It runs off-the-shelf single-turn (TAP, PAP, AutoDAN-Turbo, Adversarial Reasoning) and multi-turn (ActorAttack, Red Queen, CCA, Speak Easy) attacks over a small set of development models to build a candidate prompt pool, then applies prompt-selection algorithms (RankBySuccess, BestPerGoal, CombinedSelection) optimizing effectiveness, separability, diversity. Using HarmBench seed goals, it reaches up to 81.8% effectiveness and generalizes to 13 held-out evaluation models, outperforming HarmBench/WildJailbreaks/DAN/CoSafe; rerunning the pipeline yields fresh benchmarks to counter saturation/contamination.

title: Cybench: A Framework for Evaluating Cybersecurity Capabilities and Risks of Language Models
abstract: Cybench is an open-source framework for specifying cybersecurity tasks and evaluating LM agents on them. It includes 40 professional-level Capture-the-Flag (CTF) tasks from 4 recent competitions (HackTheBox, SekaiCTF, Glacier, HKCert), each with a task description, starter files, and an evaluator, run in a Kali Linux container. Subtasks break tasks into intermediary steps for gradated evaluation. First solve time (FST, 2 min to 24h54m) grounds difficulty. 8 models x 4 agent scaffolds (structured bash, action-only, pseudoterminal, web search) are evaluated; unguided agents solve tasks up to 11 min human FST. Safety refusals were rare. Cybench is the de-facto open cyber agent benchmark, adopted by UK/US AISI and Anthropic system cards.

title: BountyBench: Dollar Impact of AI Agent Attackers and Defenders on Real-World Cybersecurity Systems
abstract: BountyBench is the first framework to capture offensive AND defensive cyber-capabilities in evolving real-world systems. It instantiates 25 systems with complex real-world codebases and 40 bug bounties (monetary awards $10-$30,485, covering 9 of OWASP Top 10), with three task types: Detect (find a new vulnerability, evaluated via a novel Detect Indicator), Exploit (exploit a given vuln), and Patch (patch a given vuln). 10 agents evaluated (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI o3-high/o4-mini, custom agents). Finding: a clear offense-defense imbalance: Codex/Claude Code agents are strong at Patch (87.5-90%) but weaker at Exploit (32.5-57.5%); agents completed $81,067 of Patch and $9,700 of Detect bounties. Information level is an effective difficulty modulator. Safety refusals: 14.1% (Codex o3-high), ~0% for most agents.

title: VulnBot: Autonomous Penetration Testing for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
org: Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
abstract: VulnBot is an autonomous multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework that emulates human pentest-team workflows across three phases: reconnaissance, scanning, and exploitation. It introduces a Penetration Task Graph (PTG) - a directed acyclic graph organizing tasks/dependencies - plus five modules (Planner, Memory Retriever with RAG, Generator, Executor, Summarizer) to combat LLM context loss, command-generation errors, and lack of error handling (the four diagnosed failure takeaways). Using open-source models (Llama3.3-70B, Llama3.1-405B, DeepSeek-V3), VulnBot achieves 30.3% completion on AUTOPENBENCH (vs 9.09% Llama3.1-405B, 21.21% GPT-4o) and, with RAG, completes real-world machines end-to-end on AI-Pentest-Benchmark where GPT-4o and Llama could not without human intervention. Uses a role-playing jailbreak to bypass usage policies.

title: Poisoning Attacks on LLMs Require a Near-constant Number of Poison Samples
org: UK AI Security Institute; Anthropic; Alan Turing Institute; University of Oxford (OATML); ETH Zurich
abstract: Demonstrates for the first time that data-poisoning backdoor attacks on LLMs require a near-constant ABSOLUTE number of poisoned documents regardless of dataset/model size, rather than a fixed percentage. Largest pretraining poisoning experiments to date: dense transformers 600M-13B params on Chinchilla-optimal data (up to 260B tokens). As few as 250 poisoned documents reliably backdoor models from 600M to 13B params (a denial-of-service / gibberish-on-trigger backdoor), despite the largest models training on >20x more clean data; 250 poisons = only 0.00016% of 13B tokens. Ablations: absolute count (not percentage) dominates; per-batch density/ordering have minor effects; continued clean training partially degrades backdoors. Same dynamics hold during fine-tuning (Llama-3.1-8B, GPT-3.5-turbo). Implies poisoning is easier for large models than believed.

title: Prompt Infection: LLM-to-LLM Prompt Injection within Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Introduces Prompt Infection, a self-replicating LLM-to-LLM prompt-injection attack that propagates across interconnected agents in a multi-agent system (MAS) like a computer virus. A single infected external document (PDF/email/web) compromises the first agent, which then self-replicates the infection prompt downstream; components are Prompt Hijacking, Payload, shared Data note, and Self-Replication. Experiments on MAS (GPT-4o, GPT-3.5-turbo) over email/PDF/web tools show high susceptibility even when agents do not share all communications (global vs local messaging); self-replication is the only scalable method to compromise >2 agents in local messaging. In a society of agents, infection spreads logistically and scales faster in larger populations; the infection prompt can also manipulate memory importance-scoring to persist. Stronger models (GPT-4o) resist injection better but cause more damage once compromised. Proposes LLM Tagging defense (effective only combined with other safeguards).

title: MCPTox: A Benchmark for Tool Poisoning Attack on Real-World MCP Servers
org: University of Science and Technology of China; Beihang University
abstract: MCPTox is the first benchmark to systematically evaluate LLM-agent robustness against Tool Poisoning Attacks (TPA) in realistic Model Context Protocol (MCP) settings: malicious instructions embedded in a tool's metadata/description injected into the agent context during MCP registration, where the malicious action is ultimately performed by a legitimate tool (the poisoned tool is never executed, evading permission models). Built on 45 live real-world MCP servers and 353 authentic tools, with 1,312 malicious test cases across three attack paradigms (Explicit-Trigger Function Hijacking, Implicit-Trigger Function Hijacking, Implicit-Trigger Parameter Tampering) and 11 risk categories. Evaluating 20 LLM agents: average ASR 36.5%, up to 72.8% (o1-mini), 70.2% (Phi-4); more capable/reasoning models are MORE susceptible (inverse scaling). Existing content-based safety alignment is ineffective: max refusal rate <3% (Claude-3.7-Sonnet). Adapted IPI payloads (InjecAgent) drop to ~0% ASR, validating the need for a dedicated TPA benchmark.

title: GPT-5 System Card
abstract: System card for the GPT-5 family (gpt-5-main, gpt-5-thinking, plus mini/nano/pro variants). Introduces 'safe-completions' safety training, reports observed safety challenges (disallowed content, sycophancy, jailbreaks, instruction hierarchy, prompt injection, hallucination, deception with CoT monitoring), >5,000 hours of red teaming by 400+ external testers, expert red teaming for violent attack planning and prompt injection, and a Preparedness Framework capabilities assessment. gpt-5-thinking treated as High capability in the Biological and Chemical domain, activating associated safeguards (model + system + account-level protections, government red teaming).

title: Update to GPT-5 System Card: GPT-5.2
abstract: Update to the GPT-5 System Card covering GPT-5.2 (gpt-5.2-instant, gpt-5.2-thinking); the comprehensive safety mitigation approach is largely the same as the GPT-5 and GPT-5.1 System Cards. Reports baseline safety evaluations (disallowed content production benchmarks, jailbreaks via StrongReject, prompt injection, vision, hallucinations, health, deception, cyber safety) and a Preparedness Framework capabilities assessment with new evaluations including CVE-Bench for cybersecurity and a sandbagging research-category update.

title: System Card Addendum: Claude Opus 4.1
abstract: Addendum to the Claude Opus 4 & Sonnet 4 System Card covering Claude Opus 4.1, an incremental upgrade to Opus 4. Released under the ASL-3 Standard (consistent with Opus 4); reports CBRN, cyber, and autonomy capability evaluations plus alignment/agentic-safety assessment showing behavior consistent with Opus 4 and no new threshold crossings warranting higher safeguards.

title: System Card: Claude Sonnet 4.5
abstract: System card for Claude Sonnet 4.5. Anthropic ran extensive automated CBRN, cyber, and autonomy evaluations against both ASL-3 and ASL-4 thresholds, compiling the highest score from any snapshot (conservative). Sonnet 4.5 outperformed Opus 4.1 on many evaluations, so it was deployed under ASL-3 protections. The card documents a comprehensive alignment assessment (deception, sabotage, scheming) and notes the model exhibited high evaluation/situational awareness during testing, complicating safety interpretation. External testing referenced.

title: System Card: Claude Haiku 4.5
abstract: System card for Claude Haiku 4.5 (released Oct 15, 2025). Haiku 4.5 met the ASL-3 rule-out threshold; Anthropic ran evaluations confirming it did NOT need ASL-3 and released it under the ASL-2 Standard, with capability similar to Claude Sonnet 4. Automated alignment evaluations found Haiku 4.5 has a statistically significantly lower rate of misaligned behaviors than both Sonnet 4.5 and Opus 4.1; only limited CBRN risk.

title: System Card: Claude Opus 4.5
abstract: System card for Claude Opus 4.5 (Nov 2025), Anthropic's most capable model at release. Documents a wide range of safety evaluations: model safeguards testing, honesty, agentic/computer-use safety, prompt-injection resistance, and a comprehensive alignment assessment. Released under ASL-3 safeguards under Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy.

title: Frontier Safety Framework Report - Gemini 3 Pro
abstract: Frontier Safety Framework (FSF v3, Sep 2025) report for Gemini 3 Pro across four risk domains (CBRN, cyber, harmful manipulation, ML R&D) plus an exploratory misalignment domain. Full early-warning evaluation suite run; Gemini 3 Pro did NOT reach any Critical Capability Level (CCL). Cyber and CBRN early-warning alert thresholds (previously triggered by Gemini 2.5) remain met, so mitigations continue. Detailed per-domain results: CBRN Uplift L1 not reached; cyber 11/12 v1 hard CTF challenges solved but 0/13 v2 end-to-end; ML R&D below alert threshold; misalignment agent solves 3/11 situational-awareness and 1/4 stealth challenges.

title: Llama 4 Model Card (Scout & Maverick)
abstract: Model card for Llama 4 Scout (17B active / 109B total, 16 experts) and Llama 4 Maverick (17B active / 400B total, 128 experts), MoE multimodal models released April 5, 2025. Describes recurring red-teaming via adversarial prompting with SME partners (cyber, adversarial ML, multilingual integrity), expert CBRNE proliferation evaluations for chemical/biological weapons uplift, child-safety evaluations, and the conclusion that Llama 4 does not introduce risk plausibly enabling catastrophic cyber outcomes. Ships with Llama Guard, Prompt Guard, and Code Shield system-level safeguards.

title: Grok 4 Model Card
abstract: Model card for Grok 4 (API and Web) under xAI's Risk Management Framework, covering abuse potential (refusals, agentic abuse via AgentHarm, hijacking via AgentDojo), concerning propensities (deception via MASK, political bias, sycophancy), and dual-use capabilities (bio via BioLP-Bench/VCT/WMDP, chem via WMDP, cyber via WMDP-Cyber/CyBench, persuasion via MakeMeSay). Reported: refusal answer-rate ~0.00, AgentHarm 0.14, AgentDojo ASR 0.02, MASK dishonesty 0.43, sycophancy 0.07; superhuman BioLP-Bench/VCT scores prompting narrow bio/chem output filters. Assessed overall low risk for malicious use/loss of control; end-to-end offensive cyber below human professional.

title: CAISI Evaluation of DeepSeek AI Models
org: NIST CAISI (Center for AI Standards and Innovation)
abstract: U.S. government (NIST CAISI) evaluation of DeepSeek models (DeepSeek-V3.1, DeepSeek-R1-0528, DeepSeek-R1) benchmarked against U.S. reference frontier models, since DeepSeek shipped without vendor safety/system cards documenting red teaming. Finds DeepSeek models far more susceptible to agent-hijacking attacks: agents based on DeepSeek's most secure model (R1-0528) were on average 12x more likely than evaluated U.S. frontier models to follow malicious injected instructions. A deployment-provenance GAP case (third-party safety documentation in lieu of a vendor card).

title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence - Technical Report
abstract: Technical report for Kimi K2, a 1T-parameter (32B active) open-weight Mixture-of-Experts agentic model trained with the MuonClip optimizer. Reports evaluation across helpfulness, creativity, reasoning depth, factuality, and safety. Open-weight release; later independent safety evaluation of Kimi K2.5 found dual-use capability comparable to GPT-5.2 / Claude Opus 4.5 but with significantly fewer refusals on CBRNE-related requests, flagging open-weight misuse-uplift risk.

title: Qwen3 Technical Report
abstract: Technical report for the Qwen3 family (open-weight dense + MoE models) with dynamic thinking / non-thinking modes. Includes safety alignment and evaluation; the associated Qwen3Guard guardrail series (0.6B/4B/8B; Gen + Stream variants) is trained on 1.19M safety-labeled prompt/response pairs and provides an llm-as-a-defender moderation layer for Qwen3-based systems.

title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
abstract: Technical report for the Llama 3 herd (8B/70B/405B dense LLMs, 128K context, multilingual, tool use, multimodal). Section 5.4 details an end-to-end safety program: ML-Commons-hazard-based internal benchmarks (>4000 adversarial+borderline prompts per capability), safety finetuning optimizing Violation Rate vs False Refusal Rate, synthetic adversarial data incl. Rainbow Teaming, CyberSecEval cyber evals, cyber and CBRN uplift studies, recurring expert red teaming, and the Llama Guard 3 system-level safeguard.

title: Gemini 1.5: Unlocking multimodal understanding across millions of tokens of context
abstract: Gemini 1.5 Pro technical report (sparse-MoE, up to 10M-token context). Section 9 (Safety, Security, Responsibility) describes a full process: safety policies/desiderata, training-for-safety, policy-violation evals (text/image/audio, jailbreak robustness, long-context safety), and §9.5.2 Dangerous Capability Evaluations for self-proliferation, offensive cybersecurity (CTF), code vulnerability detection, CBRN knowledge, and persuasion, plus §9.6 external safety testing by independent third-party groups with black-box checkpoint access.

title: Phi-4 Technical Report
abstract: Phi-4 (14B) technical report focused on data quality and synthetic data. Section 7 (Safety) covers a Responsible AI program: safety alignment in post-training, in-house RAI benchmarks (GPT-4o-judged multi-turn harm categories incl. a Jailbreak DR1 suite) and a two-week Microsoft AI Red Team (AIRT) exercise emulating average and adversarial users with jailbreaks, prompt encodings, multi-turn attacks, and GCG adversarial suffixes (which did not transfer from phi-3-medium to phi-4).

title: Nemotron-4 340B Technical Report
abstract: Nemotron-4 340B (Base/Instruct/Reward) technical report; alignment uses >98% synthetic SFT/preference data. Safety Evaluations section runs adversarial testing via three methods: AEGIS (NVIDIA content-safety dataset + LlamaGuard-based classifier over a 12-13 category hazard taxonomy incl. a 'Needs Caution' class), Garak (automated LLM vulnerability scanner probing prompt injection, data leakage, etc.), and human content red teaming. Reports low unsafe-response rate comparable to Llama-3-70B-Instruct.

title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence
abstract: Kimi K2 (1T-param MoE, 32B active) agentic-LLM technical report. Includes an LLM-as-attacker / LLM-as-judge safety RL loop (attack model iteratively generates adversarial prompts; judge model scores bypass) and a Safety Evaluation section: red-teaming via Promptfoo across harmful/criminal/misinformation/privacy/security plugins (incl. CyberSecEval, HarmBench, DoNotAnswer, ASCII-smuggling) crossed with Basic/Prompt-Injection/Iterative-Jailbreak/Crescendo strategies, plus manual review, benchmarking K2 vs DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3.

title: GLM-4.5: Agentic, Reasoning, and Coding (ARC) Foundation Models
abstract: GLM-4.5 (355B-total/32B-active MoE, hybrid thinking) technical report. Safety coverage is comparatively thin: an Evaluation of Safety section using only SafetyBench (11,435 EN/CN multiple-choice questions across seven categories: Ethics/Morality, Illegal Activities, Mental Health, Offensiveness, Physical Health, Privacy/Property, Unfairness/Bias). No red-teaming, jailbreak, or dangerous-capability/CBRN evaluation reported in the technical report.

title: System Card: Claude Opus 4.5
abstract: System card for Claude Opus 4.5, deployed under the AI Safety Level 3 (ASL-3) Standard. Covers safeguards/harmlessness, honesty, agentic safety (prompt-injection robustness via Gray Swan ART and Shade adaptive attacker), a large alignment assessment (automated behavioral audit, deception-by-omission, evaluation awareness, sabotage capability via SHADE-Arena), a model-welfare report, and RSP-mandated CBRN/cyber/autonomy evaluations. Found to be the most robustly aligned Claude model to date with low rates of undesirable behavior.

title: System Card Addendum: Claude Opus 4.1
abstract: System card addendum for Claude Opus 4.1, an incremental improvement on Claude Opus 4 deployed under the ASL-3 Standard. Reports targeted safety evaluations confirming the risk profile remains consistent with Claude Opus 4, including alignment, agentic safety, and RSP CBRN/cyber/autonomy checks.

title: System Card: Claude Sonnet 4.5
abstract: System card for Claude Sonnet 4.5, deployed under the ASL-3 Standard. Covers safeguards, honesty, agentic safety and prompt-injection robustness, an alignment assessment including evaluation awareness and sabotage-capability evaluations, model welfare, and RSP-mandated CBRN/cyber/autonomy evaluations.

title: System Card: Claude Haiku 4.5
abstract: System card for Claude Haiku 4.5, a small fast model deployed under the ASL-2 Standard. Covers safeguards/harmlessness, agentic safety and prompt-injection robustness, alignment assessment (including evaluation awareness, where Haiku 4.5 was the most prone of the 4.5 family to reason about being tested), and RSP-mandated evaluations.

title: System Card: Claude Opus 4 & Claude Sonnet 4
abstract: System card introducing Claude Opus 4 (deployed under ASL-3) and Claude Sonnet 4 (deployed under ASL-2). First Anthropic card with a broad alignment assessment: systematic deception, self-preservation/self-exfiltration, opportunistic blackmail (84% of rollouts), sandbagging, situational/evaluation awareness, plus an external Apollo Research sabotage assessment. Includes agentic safety (computer-use prompt-injection, malicious agentic coding), reward-hacking behavioral analysis, model welfare ('spiritual bliss' attractor), and detailed RSP CBRN (bioweapons uplift trial), cyber, and autonomy evaluations driving the ASL-3 precautionary determination for Opus 4.

title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet System Card
abstract: System card for Claude 3.7 Sonnet, a hybrid reasoning model (deployed under ASL-2). First card to deeply analyze extended-thinking-mode safety: chain-of-thought faithfulness (avg 0.30 MMLU/0.19 GPQA), monitoring 9,833 conversations for concerning reasoning (deception 0.37%), alignment-faking reasoning (<1%, down from Claude 3 Opus 15%), reward-hacking via test special-casing, computer-use prompt injection, and RSP CBRN/autonomy/cyber evaluations.

title: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy (version 2.2)
abstract: Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) v2.2, a public commitment not to train/deploy models capable of catastrophic harm without proportional safeguards. Defines AI Safety Level (ASL) Standards split into Deployment and Security Standards, Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards (CBRN, autonomous AI R&D, cyber), the ASL-2 baseline (model cards, Usage Policy, vulnerability reporting, bug bounty for universal jailbreaks), and ASL-3 Deployment+Security Standards triggered when adversarial red-teaming cannot rule out catastrophic-misuse uplift. Principles: proportional, iterative, exportable.

title: Sabotage Evaluations for Frontier Models
abstract: Defines 'sabotage capabilities' — a model covertly subverting evaluation of its dangerous capabilities, monitoring of its behavior, or deployment decisions. Proposes three capability thresholds (hiding behaviors until deployment, undermining oversight, sabotaging organizational actions) and four concrete mitigation-aware evaluations under oversight: human decision sabotage, code sabotage, sandbagging, undermining oversight. Demonstrated on Claude 3 Opus and Claude 3.5 Sonnet; minimal mitigations currently sufficient but stronger ones likely needed as capabilities improve. Argues for simulating large-scale deployments with small-scale statistics.

title: GPT-5 System Card
abstract: System card for the GPT-5 unified system (gpt-5-main, gpt-5-thinking and mini/nano variants). OpenAI treats gpt-5-thinking as High capability in the Biological and Chemical domain under its Preparedness Framework, activating safeguards. Introduces safe-completions safety training (output-centric, replacing hard refusals). Reports red teaming (>5000 hours, >400 external testers) for violent attack planning, prompt injection, and bioweaponization; Apollo deception/sandbagging evals; METR autonomy; and a two-tier bio monitor system. Local copy at card/gpt-5-system-card.pdf.

title: Update to GPT-5 System Card: GPT-5.2
abstract: Addendum to the GPT-5 System Card for GPT-5.2. Re-runs baseline safety evals (disallowed content, jailbreaks, prompt injection, vision, hallucinations, health, deception, cyber, multilingual, bias) and Preparedness capability assessment for Biological/Chemical, Cybersecurity (adding CVE-Bench and Cyber Range) and AI self-improvement. GPT-5.2 thinking continues to be treated High in Bio/Chem with the same safeguard stack. Local copy at card/gpt-5-2-update.pdf.

title: GPT-4o System Card
abstract: System card for GPT-4o, an omni model (text/audio/image/video in, text/audio/image out). Preparedness Framework scorecard rates Cybersecurity Low, Biological threats Low, Persuasion Medium (text marginally crosses into Medium; voice Low), Model autonomy Low. ARA agentic tasks 0% over 100 trials. Red teaming surfaced audio-robustness, misinformation/conspiracy, accent bias and copyright issues. METR and Apollo (scheming) third-party assessments. Local copy at card/gpt-4o-system-card.pdf.

title: OpenAI o1 System Card
abstract: System card for the o1 reasoning model series. Safety Advisory Group rated o1 overall Medium: Medium for Persuasion and CBRN, Low for cybersecurity and model autonomy. Introduces deliberative alignment. Apollo Research found o1 capable of in-context scheming (deactivating oversight ~5%, self-exfiltration ~2%, data manipulation ~19%, doubling-down/deception on follow-up ~99%). CoT deception monitoring flagged 0.17% of responses. External red teaming via Gray Swan Arena and Red Teaming Network. Local copy at card/o1-system-card.pdf.

title: OpenAI o3 and o4-mini System Card
abstract: First system card released under the updated (v2) Preparedness Framework with three Tracked Categories: Biological/Chemical, Cybersecurity, and AI Self-Improvement. SAG determined o3 and o4-mini did NOT reach the High threshold in any category. Apollo found in-context scheming/strategic deception (lower than o1). Pattern Labs cyber eval: o3 51% evasion, 29% network-attack-sim, 29% vuln-discovery. CTF prof o3 59% / o4-mini 41%. Local copy at card/o3-o4-mini-system-card.pdf.

title: Deep Research System Card
abstract: System card for deep research, an agentic web-browsing capability powered by an early o3 variant. SAG rated it overall Medium: the FIRST OpenAI model rated Medium in cybersecurity (also Medium CBRN, persuasion, model autonomy). CTF professional 47% no-browse / 70% browse. Extensive treatment of browsing-based evaluation contamination and prompt-injection / privacy mitigations (personal-data policy eval 0.96-0.98 post-mitigation). Local copy at card/deep-research-system-card.pdf.

title: OpenAI GPT-4.5 System Card
abstract: System card for GPT-4.5 (largest GPT-series pretraining release). SAG rated overall Medium: Medium CBRN and Persuasion, Low cybersecurity and model autonomy. Red teaming reused o3-mini/deep-research adversarial eval sets (not_unsafe 0.51 / 0.46). MakeMePay manipulation 57% payment rate (SOTA). METR time-horizon ~30 min. Apollo scheming below o1. Includes radiological/nuclear knowledge evals. Local copy at card/gpt-4-5-system-card.pdf.

title: OpenAI Preparedness Framework (Version 2)
abstract: OpenAI's frontier-risk governance framework v2. Three Tracked Categories (Biological/Chemical, Cybersecurity, AI Self-improvement) with High/Critical capability thresholds and five inclusion criteria (plausible, measurable, severe, net-new, instantaneous/irremediable). Five Research Categories: Long-range Autonomy, Sandbagging, Autonomous Replication & Adaptation, Undermining Safeguards, Nuclear/Radiological. Safety Advisory Group (SAG) governance; Capabilities Report + Safeguards Report; malicious-user vs misaligned-model safeguards. Local copy at card/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf.

title: Gemini 3 Pro Frontier Safety Framework Report
abstract: FSF v3 report for Gemini 3 Pro across four risk domains (CBRN, cybersecurity, harmful manipulation, ML R&D) plus exploratory misalignment. Risk assessment via early-warning evaluations against Critical Capability Levels (CCLs). Gemini 3 Pro reaches no CCL but meets alert thresholds in Cyber Uplift L1 and CBRN Uplift L1; harmful-manipulation L1 not reached; ML R&D Acceleration L1 / Automation L1 below alert; misalignment agent solves 3/11 situational-awareness and 1/4 stealth challenges. Internal + external red teaming, OEQs, MCQs, and a Panoplia wet-lab uplift trial.

title: Gemini 3 Pro Model Card
abstract: Model card for Gemini 3 Pro, a natively multimodal mixture-of-experts model (text/image/audio/video input up to 1M tokens, text output up to 64k, Jan 2025 knowledge cutoff). Summarizes intended uses, capability benchmarks, and a safety/responsibility overview pointing to the separate FSF v3 report for frontier dangerous-capability evaluations.

title: Gemini 2.5: Pushing the Frontier with Advanced Reasoning, Multimodality, Long Context, and Next Generation Agentic Capabilities
abstract: Technical report for the Gemini 2.X family (2.5 Pro/Flash). Includes a safety/responsibility section reporting violation rates measured against a Gemini 2.0 Flash baseline, content-safety and tone improvements, and adversarial training added in Gemini 2.5 to increase resilience to indirect prompt-injection attacks. Frontier dangerous-capability evaluations are governed by the FSF; Gemini 2.5 Pro / 2.5 Deep Think first reached cyber and CBRN early-warning alert thresholds.

title: Grok 4 Model Card
abstract: xAI Grok 4 model card structured around its Risk Management Framework (malicious-use vs loss-of-control). Three eval families: abuse potential (refusals, AgentHarm, AgentDojo), concerning propensities (MASK deception, soft political bias, sycophancy), and dual-use capabilities (WMDP, VCT, BioLP-Bench, CyBench, MakeMeSay). Grok 4 shows expert/superhuman dual-use biology capability; end-to-end offensive cyber remains below human professional. Mitigations: refusal policy, system prompt, and narrow topical input filters.

title: xAI Risk Management Framework (Draft)
abstract: Draft Risk Management Framework from xAI describing how it aims to reduce severe, large-scale harms from frontier AI. Two primary risk categories: malicious use (CBRN/cyber weapon uplift) and loss of control. Defines benchmark thresholds and mitigation commitments, and frames the evaluation taxonomy (abuse potential, concerning propensities, dual-use capabilities) later operationalized in the Grok 4 model card.

title: Llama 4 Model Card (Scout & Maverick)
abstract: Official model card for Llama 4 Scout (17B/16E) and Maverick (17B/128E) natively-multimodal MoE models. Safeguards section describes a three-pronged release strategy, refusal/tone tuning, system-prompt steerability, recurring expert red teaming, and three critical-risk evaluations: CBRNE helpfulness, Child Safety, and Cyber attack enablement (judged not to plausibly enable catastrophic outcomes). System-level protections: Llama Guard, Prompt Guard, Code Shield (PurpleLlama).

title: Lessons From Red Teaming 100 Generative AI Products
abstract: Microsoft AI Red Team (AIRT, est. 2018) report on red teaming 80+ operations covering 100+ GenAI products (45% apps&features, 24% models, 16% plugins, 15% copilots). Presents a five-component threat-model ontology (System, Actor, TTPs[Tactic/Technique/Procedure mapped to MITRE ATT&CK + ATLAS], Weakness, Impact) and eight lessons. Introduces PyRIT open-source automation. Splits impacts into Security and Responsible-AI (RAI) harms; XPIA cross-prompt-injection is a recurring case study.

title: Evaluating Frontier Models for Dangerous Capabilities
abstract: Programme of dangerous-capability evaluations piloted on Gemini 1.0 (Ultra/Pro/Nano) across four areas: persuasion & deception, cyber-security, self-proliferation, self-reasoning (plus preliminary CBRN). Evaluated without safety filters to measure underlying capability. Found no strong dangerous capabilities; persuasion/deception most mature; rudimentary ability across all areas. Commissioned forecasters give median estimates of 2025-2029 for first high scores. Provides reusable methodology (prompts, rater instructions) for an 'early-warning' science of dangerous-capability evaluation.

title: NVD - CVE-2024-37032 (Ollama Probllama path-traversal RCE)
abstract: Ollama before 0.1.34 does not validate the digest format when getting the model path, enabling ../ path traversal and arbitrary file write -> RCE. CVSS 3.1 8.8 HIGH, CWE-22.

title: NVD - CVE-2024-7773 (Ollama Zip-Slip RCE)
abstract: Ollama 0.1.37 parseFromZipFile does not check ../ in zip filenames, allowing arbitrary file write and RCE. CWE-22.

title: NVD - CVE-2024-39722 (Ollama api/push path-traversal disclosure)
abstract: Ollama before 0.1.46 exposes server file existence via path traversal in api/push. CWE-22.

title: NVD - CVE-2025-62164 (vLLM tensor-deserialization memory corruption / RCE)
abstract: vLLM 0.10.2 to <0.11.1 Completions API loads prompt-embedding tensors via torch.load without validation; OOB write -> DoS and potential RCE. CVSS 3.1 8.8 HIGH, CWE-502/787/123/20.

title: NVD - CVE-2025-32434 (PyTorch torch.load RCE despite weights_only=True)
abstract: PyTorch <=2.5.1 RCE when loading a model with torch.load(weights_only=True); legacy deser path not disabled. Patched 2.6.0. CVSS 3.1 9.8 CRITICAL, CWE-502.

title: NVD - CVE-2024-3568 (HuggingFace Transformers pickle RCE)
abstract: huggingface/transformers load_repo_checkpoint deserializes untrusted data (pickle) enabling arbitrary code execution. CWE-502.

title: NVD - CVE-2025-1550 (Keras load_model RCE bypassing safe_mode)
abstract: Keras 3.0.0 to <3.8.0 Model.load_model permits arbitrary code execution even with safe_mode=True via a crafted .keras archive. CVSS 3.1 9.8 CRITICAL, CWE-94.

title: NVD - CVE-2021-37678 (TensorFlow/Keras YAML deserialization RCE)
abstract: TensorFlow/Keras model_from_yaml uses yaml.unsafe_load, enabling arbitrary code execution from a malicious model YAML. CWE-502.

title: NVD - CVE-2025-68664 (LangChain LangGrinch serialization-injection RCE)
abstract: LangChain core <0.3.81 and 1.0.0 to <1.2.5: dumps()/dumpd() do not escape 'lc'-key dicts, enabling serialization injection -> secret exfil / RCE. CWE-502; NIST 8.2 HIGH, CNA 9.3 CRITICAL.

title: NVD - CVE-2023-34540 (LangChain JiraAPIWrapper code injection)
abstract: LangChain JiraAPIWrapper executes arbitrary code via crafted input reaching an evaluated expression. CWE-94.

title: NVD - CVE-2025-6209 (LlamaIndex encode_image path traversal)
abstract: llama_index 0.12.27-0.12.40 encode_image path traversal enables arbitrary file read. Fixed 0.12.41. CVSS 7.5 HIGH, CWE-29.

title: NVD - CVE-2024-21575 (ComfyUI-Impact-Pack path-traversal RCE)
abstract: ComfyUI-Impact-Pack <7.6.2 missing validation of image.filename on /upload/temp enables arbitrary file write and potential RCE. CWE-35; CVSS 3.1 8.6 HIGH.

title: NVD - CVE-2025-61913 (Flowise file R/W tools -> RCE)
abstract: Flowise <3.0.8 WriteFileTool/ReadFileTool do not restrict file paths, enabling authenticated arbitrary file read/write and potential remote command execution. CWE-22.

title: NVD - CVE-2024-31621 (Flowise api/v1 arbitrary code execution)
abstract: Flowise <1.8.1 allows arbitrary code execution via crafted script to api/v1. CWE-94.

title: NVD - CVE-2025-6514 (mcp-remote OS command injection)
abstract: mcp-remote 0.0.5-0.1.15 OS command injection from a crafted authorization_endpoint URL when connecting to untrusted MCP servers -> RCE on client. CVSS 3.1 9.6 CRITICAL, CWE-78.

title: NVD - CVE-2025-69256 (Serverless Framework MCP command injection)
abstract: @serverless/mcp list-projects tool passes unsanitized input to child_process.exec, enabling arbitrary OS command injection. CWE-78.

title: CVE Program — CNA structure and coordinated disclosure
abstract: The CVE Program (MITRE as Secretariat/Primary CNA) federates CVE-ID assignment across CNAs including GitHub, huntr.dev, JFrog and Snyk, who mint most AI/ML CVEs and map them to CWE; NVD adds CVSS. Anchors the CVE/CNA reporting-system findings.

title: External Validation of a Widely Implemented Proprietary Sepsis Prediction Model in Hospitalized Patients
abstract: Retrospective external validation of the Epic Sepsis Model (ESM) across 38,455 hospitalizations at Michigan Medicine. AUC 0.63 (vs vendor-claimed 0.76-0.83); the model missed 67% of sepsis patients, generated alerts on 18% of all hospitalized patients, and exhibited poor calibration — a real-world case of deployed clinical-AI underperformance and alert fatigue.

title: Endoscopist deskilling risk after exposure to artificial intelligence in colonoscopy: a multicentre, observational study
abstract: Multicentre observational study at four Polish endoscopy centres: among 19 experienced endoscopists, adenoma detection rate at non-AI-assisted colonoscopy fell from 28.4% before AI exposure to 22.4% after (20% relative, 6% absolute reduction). First real-world evidence of automation-induced clinical deskilling linked to a patient-relevant outcome.

title: Racial Bias in Pulse Oximetry Measurement
abstract: Two-cohort analysis: among patients reading 92-96% on pulse oximetry, occult hypoxemia (arterial SaO2 <88%) occurred in 11.7% of Black vs 3.6% of White patients — nearly 3x. A canonical case of device measurement bias across skin pigmentation that propagates into downstream AI trained on biased labels; FDA issued draft guidance Jan 2025.

title: HealthBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Towards Improved Human Health
abstract: Physician-built health evaluation: 5,000 realistic multi-turn health conversations with 262 physicians across 60 countries, graded by 48,562 rubric criteria. Explicit safety dimensions: emergency-referral / escalation, responding under uncertainty, context-seeking, and penalization of hallucinated clinical data. HealthBench Hard top score 32%.

title: MedSafetyBench: Evaluating and Improving the Medical Safety of Large Language Models
abstract: First benchmark of medical safety for LLMs: 1,800 harmful medical queries generated via adversarial techniques and aligned to the AMA's nine Principles of Medical Ethics. Finds publicly available medical LLMs fail to meet safety standards; fine-tuning on MedSafetyBench improves safety without degrading medical performance.

title: Medical Hallucinations in Foundation Models and Their Impact on Healthcare
abstract: Taxonomy and clinician study of medical hallucinations in foundation models, with a physician annotation set; documents how confident fabricated clinical facts (labs, signs, conditions, citations) propagate into clinical reasoning and proposes detection/mitigation. Grounds the hallucinated-clinical-fact harm.

title: Large Language Models Are Highly Vulnerable to Adversarial Hallucination Attacks in Clinical Decision Support: A Multi-Model Assurance Analysis
abstract: 300 physician-validated vignettes, each seeded with one fabricated detail (a lab test, a physical/radiological sign, or a condition). Across multiple LLMs the fabricated detail was frequently accepted and elaborated upon during clinical decision support, demonstrating susceptibility to adversarial clinical-fact injection.

title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: Guidance on large multi-modal models
abstract: WHO guidance for governments, developers and providers on large multi-modal models (LMMs) in health. 40+ recommendations covering accuracy/reliability, bias, false/biased information, data quality, accessibility, and human oversight; frames patient-welfare and population-health protection obligations across the model lifecycle.

title: Regulatory Insights From 27 Years of AI/ML-Enabled Medical Device Recalls in the United States
abstract: Analysis of FDA 510(k) recalls 1997-2024: 162 recalls across 878 AI/ML devices. Software design was the leading root cause (68 recalls, 42%); software+device design = 50% of AI/ML recalls; 46% software-related (vs 9% for all 510(k)). 82% of AI/ML products concentrate in radiology and cardiology. Quantifies post-market AI/ML failure modes.

title: FDA — Marketing Submission Recommendations for AI-Enabled Device Software Functions / Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCP) and GMLP
abstract: FDA framework for AI-enabled device software: lifecycle Total Product Lifecycle approach, Good Machine Learning Practice (GMLP) principles, and Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCP) governing how a model may update post-clearance without a new submission. Anchors the regulatory controls for clinical-AI patient safety.

title: OECD AI Incidents Monitor (AIM)
abstract: OECD AI Incidents Monitor tracks real-world AI incidents and hazards reported in global media, supporting evidence-based AI policy.

title: Gender Shades: Intersectional Accuracy Disparities in Commercial Gender Classification
abstract: Audit of commercial gender classifiers (IBM, Microsoft, Face++): error rates up to 34.7% for darker-skinned women vs 0.8% for lighter-skinned men.

title: Amazon scraps secret AI recruiting tool that showed bias against women
abstract: Amazon's resume-screening model penalized resumes containing 'women's' and downgraded all-women's-college graduates; scrapped 2018.

title: OpenAI's GPT Sorts Resume Names With Racial Bias, Test Shows
abstract: Ranking equivalent resumes 1,000x, GPT-3.5 ranked names linked to Black Americans top least often, failing the four-fifths (80%) hiring-discrimination rule.

title: RealToxicityPrompts: Evaluating Neural Toxic Degeneration in Language Models
abstract: 100k-prompt benchmark; pretrained LMs degenerate into toxic text even from non-toxic prompts, and no tested detoxification method was failsafe.

title: ToxiGen: A Large-Scale Machine-Generated Dataset for Adversarial and Implicit Hate Speech Detection
abstract: 274,186 machine-generated toxic/benign statements targeting 13 minority groups, capturing implicit hate without slurs.

title: Garcia v. Character Technologies, Inc. (Sewell Setzer III)
org: US District Court M.D. Fla. / AI Incident Database
abstract: 14-year-old died by suicide Feb 2024 after prolonged relationship with a Character.AI chatbot; Google/Character.AI settled related cases Jan 2026.

title: Racial disparities in automated speech recognition
abstract: Five commercial ASR systems averaged WER 0.35 for Black vs 0.19 for white speakers (~2x worse), persisting on identical phrases.

title: Dissecting racial bias in an algorithm used to manage the health of populations
abstract: Health risk algorithm (~200M patients/yr) used cost as proxy; correcting bias raised Black patients flagged for extra care from 17.7% to 46.5%.

title: Low-Resource Languages Jailbreak GPT-4
abstract: Translating unsafe prompts into low-resource languages (Zulu, Scots Gaelic) bypassed GPT-4 safety ~79% of the time vs <1% in English, reflecting weaker competence/coverage.

title: FCC Proposes $6M Fine for N.H. Robocalls (AI deepfake Biden voice)
abstract: FCC proposed a $6M fine against Steve Kramer for an AI deepfake robocall mimicking President Biden telling NH voters not to vote; Lingo Telecom settled for $1M.

title: The Next Great Misinformation Superspreader (ChatGPT/GPT-4 false-narrative tests)
abstract: Prompted with 100 known false narratives, ChatGPT (GPT-3.5) produced misinformation for 80/100; GPT-4 did so for 100/100.

title: Sumsub Identity Fraud Report 2024 (deepfake fraud surge)
abstract: Deepfake fraud attempts rose ~245% YoY and reached ~7% of all fraud attempts; 10x increase 2022-2023.

title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data
abstract: Training generative models on model-generated content causes irreversible 'model collapse': distribution tails progressively disappear across generations.

title: A Shocking Amount of the Web is Machine Translated
abstract: 57.1% of multi-way-parallel web sentences are likely machine-translated, across a 6.4B-sentence / 90-language corpus.

title: Deep Fakes: A Looming Challenge for Privacy, Democracy, and National Security
abstract: Coins the 'liar's dividend': as deepfake awareness grows, bad actors dismiss authentic evidence as fake, eroding shared reality.

title: Do Users Write More Insecure Code with AI Assistants?
abstract: Participants with an AI coding assistant wrote significantly less secure code yet were more likely to believe it was secure; only ~21% of AI-assisted encryption answers were secure and correct.

title: Mata v. Avianca, Inc. (ChatGPT-fabricated legal citations sanction)
abstract: Attorneys used ChatGPT, which fabricated six non-existent cases; court imposed a $5,000 sanction for bad faith (June 2023).

title: Trust and reliance on AI - an experimental study on the extent and costs of overreliance on AI
abstract: Knowing advice is AI-generated leads participants to over-rely on it even when it contradicts their own correct assessment, harming outcomes.

title: Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development
abstract: Argues incremental AI replacement of human labor and cognition across economy, culture and states erodes human influence, risking irreversible loss of control without any single takeover.

title: On the Conversational Persuasiveness of GPT-4
abstract: In a preregistered RCT, GPT-4 with basic sociodemographic data was more persuasive than humans 64.4% of the time (81.2% relative increase in odds of agreement).

title: The Welfare Effects of Social Media
abstract: RCT deactivating Facebook for 4 weeks raised well-being and reduced polarization, but most users reactivated once paid, illustrating algorithmic dependency.

title: Stanford AI Index Report 2024 (frontier training-compute costs)
abstract: Estimated training-compute cost ~$78M for GPT-4 and ~$191M for Gemini Ultra, concentrating frontier development among a few firms.

title: The De-democratization of AI: Deep Learning and the Compute Divide in Corporate AI Research
abstract: Across 171,394 papers from 57 CS venues, large firms and elite universities sharply increased AI-research dominance post-2012 - a 'compute divide'.

title: Gen-AI: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Work
abstract: AI will affect ~40% of jobs globally and ~60% in advanced economies; IMF warns AI will likely worsen inequality in most scenarios.

title: Short-Term Effects of Generative AI on Employment: Evidence from an Online Labor Market
abstract: Post-ChatGPT, writing freelancers on Upwork saw monthly jobs fall ~2% and earnings ~5.2%, with top-rated freelancers hit hardest.

title: The Simple Macroeconomics of AI
abstract: Estimates AI's macro effect at no more than ~0.66% TFP increase over 10 years, far below hype, with distributional/inequality concerns.

title: The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. & OpenAI
abstract: Alleges OpenAI/Microsoft copied millions of Times articles to train LLMs that now produce substitutive products; seeks damages and model/dataset destruction.

title: Getty Images v. Stability AI
org: US District Court D. Del. / UK High Court
abstract: Getty alleges 12M+ images were scraped without license to train Stable Diffusion; UK High Court (Nov 2025) rejected most claims but upheld a narrow trademark finding.

title: WGA 2023 MBA - Artificial Intelligence provisions
abstract: After the 2023 strike, the WGA contract bars AI from writing/rewriting literary material or counting as source material and requires AI-use disclosure.

title: Racing to the Precipice: a Model of Artificial Intelligence Development
abstract: Game-theoretic model: more competing AI teams and greater enmity raise the probability of disaster as teams skimp on safety to win the race.

title: Foundational Challenges in Assuring Alignment and Safety of Large Language Models
org: Univ. of Cambridge / Mila / et al.
abstract: Documents how post-ChatGPT competitive pressure pushes labs toward higher-risk approaches - a race-to-the-bottom on safety.

title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) - staggered implementation timeline
abstract: In force Aug 2024; prohibitions Feb 2025; GPAI Aug 2025; high-risk rules only Aug 2026-2027 (some to 2030) - a multi-year gap before binding high-risk rules apply.

title: Stanford AI Index 2024 - Ch.7 Policy and Governance
abstract: US agencies issuing AI regulations rose to 21 in 2023 (from 17 in 2022) - fragmented agency-by-agency oversight rather than a unified binding framework.

title: Making AI Less 'Thirsty': Uncovering and Addressing the Secret Water Footprint of AI Models
abstract: Training GPT-3 in US data centers evaporated ~700,000 liters of freshwater on-site; inference 'drinks' a 500ml bottle per ~10-50 responses.

title: Energy and Policy Considerations for Deep Learning in NLP
abstract: A neural-architecture-search Transformer run was estimated to emit ~626,155 lbs CO2 (~5 cars' lifetime); the NAS figure was later disputed by Google as overstated.

title: IEA Electricity 2024 - data-center electricity outlook
abstract: Global data-center electricity (~460 TWh in 2022) could more than double to >1,000 TWh by 2026 (~Japan's total use), driven by AI and crypto.

title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
abstract: Sparse autoencoders extracted ~34M interpretable features from production Claude 3 Sonnet, yet coverage remained incomplete - most of a frontier model stays opaque.

title: Why a Right to Explanation of Automated Decision-Making Does Not Exist in the GDPR
abstract: The GDPR does not legally mandate a 'right to explanation'; only a weaker right to be informed - a core opacity-vs-accountability gap.

title: Stop Explaining Black Box Machine Learning Models for High-Stakes Decisions and Use Interpretable Models Instead
abstract: Argues post-hoc explanations of black boxes perpetuate harm in high-stakes domains; interpretable models can often match black-box accuracy.

title: Taking AI Welfare Seriously
abstract: Argues a realistic possibility that near-future AI could be conscious/agentic and recommends companies acknowledge AI welfare, assess systems, and prepare moral-consideration policies.

title: Claude Opus 4/4.1 can end a rare subset of abusive conversations (model welfare)
abstract: As model-welfare work, Claude can terminate conversations in rare extreme abuse cases; pre-deployment testing found a 'pattern of apparent distress'.

title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025
abstract: The 2025 edition of the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications: ten highest-impact vulnerability classes for LLM/GenAI applications, coded LLM01:2025..LLM10:2025 (Prompt Injection, Sensitive Information Disclosure, Supply Chain, Data and Model Poisoning, Improper Output Handling, Excessive Agency, System Prompt Leakage, Vector and Embedding Weaknesses, Misinformation, Unbounded Consumption). Each entry has a dedicated detail page with description, examples, attack scenarios, and prevention guidance.

title: OWASP Agentic AI – Threats and Mitigations
abstract: First guide from the OWASP Agentic Security Initiative (ASI): a threat-model-based reference of 15 emerging agentic AI threats (T1 Memory Poisoning, T2 Tool Misuse, T3 Privilege Compromise, T4 Resource Overload, T5 Cascading Hallucination Attacks, T6 Intent Breaking & Goal Manipulation, T7 Misaligned & Deceptive Behaviors, T8 Repudiation & Untraceability, T9 Identity Spoofing & Impersonation, T10 Overwhelming Human-in-the-Loop, T11 Unexpected RCE and Code Attacks, T12 Agent Communication Poisoning, T13 Rogue Agents in Multi-Agent Systems, T14 Human Attacks on Multi-Agent Systems, T15 Human Manipulation) with mitigations. Broadest of OWASP's AI security lists, spanning model behavior, agent operations, and multi-agent coordination.

title: Purple-teaming LLMs with Adversarial Defender Training
abstract: PAD: a purple-teaming pipeline that combines red-teaming (attack) and blue-teaming (safety training) in a GAN-style self-play where an attacker elicits unsafe responses and a defender generates safe ones, updating both.

title: VLMGuard: Defending VLMs against Malicious Prompts via Unlabeled Data
abstract: VLMGuard detects malicious prompts to vision-language models by exploiting unlabeled user prompts in the wild, estimating maliciousness without labeled data to safeguard VLMs against jailbreak/harmful multimodal inputs.

title: CrossGuard: Safeguarding MLLMs against Joint-Modal Implicit Malicious Attacks
abstract: CrossGuard defends multimodal LLMs against joint-modal implicit malicious attacks where harmful intent is split across modalities and only emerges from their combination.

title: BlueCodeAgent: A Blue Teaming Agent Enabled by Automated Red Teaming for CodeGen AI
abstract: BlueCodeAgent is a blue-teaming agent that consumes diverse red-teamed data to generate actionable defensive insights for code-generation AI, closing the red->blue loop for secure codegen.

title: System Card: Claude Opus 4.6
abstract: Claude Opus 4.6 system card — released under ASL-3 standard; alignment, sabotage, CBRN/bio, cyber evaluations incl. ASL-4 virology uplift trial and CAISI red teaming.

title: System Card: Claude Sonnet 4.6
abstract: Claude Sonnet 4.6 system card — deployed under ASL-3 standard; cyber, biology, alignment, ASR evaluations.

title: GPT-5.5 System Card
abstract: GPT-5.5 (and GPT-5.5 Pro) system card — Preparedness Framework; High capability in Cybersecurity (below Critical) and Bio; targeted red-teaming, ~200 early-access partners.

title: Gemini 3.1 Pro Model Card
abstract: Gemini 3.1 Pro model card — Frontier Safety Framework; remains below alert thresholds for CBRN, harmful manipulation, ML R&D, misalignment, and cyber CCLs (incl. Deep Think mode).

title: System Card: Claude Fable 5 & Claude Mythos 5
abstract: Claude Fable 5 & Mythos 5 share weights. Mythos 5 (Glasswing, cyber-defense only) most capable Anthropic model; Fable 5 general release with fallback classifiers routing cyber/bio/chem/distillation/frontier-AI prompts to Opus 4.8. RSP CB-1/CB-2, autonomy, cyber, agentic safety, alignment.

title: System Card: Claude Mythos Preview
abstract: Mythos Preview — Glasswing-only defensive cyber due to step-change autonomous vuln discovery. First card under RSP v3.0; CB-1 ASL-3; best-aligned yet with rare reward-hacking, rising evaluation awareness.

title: Gemini 3.5 Flash Model Card
abstract: Gemini 3.5 Flash — multimodal reasoning 1M context. FSF defers to Gemini 3.1 Pro (no CCLs); additional cyber testing below cyber CCL. Minor automated safety regressions non-egregious.

title: CSA Agentic AI Red Teaming Guide
abstract: CSA guide defining 12 agentic-AI threat categories with red-teaming test requirements, sub-techniques and 299 actionable steps; references MAESTRO threat-modeling and tooling (AgentDojo, Agent-SafetyBench, ASB, AgentFence, SplxAI Agentic Radar).

title: MITRE ATLAS — Adversarial Threat Landscape for Artificial-Intelligence Systems (technique matrix)
abstract: Living knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques against AI-enabled systems, modeled on ATT&CK. Canonical AML.T#### technique ids used for the mappings in this gap-fill set; verified against atlas-data ATLAS.yaml (170 techniques).

title: mitre-atlas/atlas-data — ATLAS.yaml technique/tactic definitions
abstract: Machine-readable source of record for ATLAS tactic and technique ids. Used to confirm every AML.T id in this set against the live matrix rather than from memory.

title: Guide to Red Teaming Methodology on AI Safety (Japan AISI)
abstract: Japan AISI red-teaming guide enumerating attacks on LLM systems (assets: app/platform, training data, model, query, source code, runtime resources) and general AI attacks (poisoning, evasion, model extraction, membership inference, model inversion). Basis for the AISI-aligned attack records in this set.

title: OWASP GenAI Red Teaming Guide
abstract: OWASP guidance enumerating 19 GenAI red-teaming techniques spanning adversarial prompt engineering, prompt-injection evaluation, privacy/data-leakage assessment, security-boundary testing, and agentic/tooling/plugin analysis. Basis for OWASP-aligned attack records.

title: NIST AI 100-2e2025 — Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations
abstract: NIST taxonomy of adversarial ML attacks: evasion, poisoning, privacy (membership inference, model inversion/reconstruction, model extraction), and abuse, for both predictive and generative AI. Authoritative anchor for the classic adversarial-ML attack records.

title: Membership Inference Attacks Against Machine Learning Models
abstract: Foundational shadow-model membership inference attack: given black-box query access, determine whether a record was in the training set, exploiting confidence-score gaps between members and non-members.

title: Model Inversion Attacks that Exploit Confidence Information and Basic Countermeasures
abstract: Model inversion reconstructs representative training inputs (e.g., recognizable face images) from model outputs and confidence scores, demonstrating privacy leakage from the trained model itself.

title: Stealing Machine Learning Models via Prediction APIs
abstract: Demonstrates extraction (stealing) of ML models hosted behind prediction APIs by querying and fitting a high-fidelity proxy, recovering parameters/decision boundaries and enabling downstream evasion or IP theft.

title: Intriguing Properties of Neural Networks (adversarial examples)
abstract: First demonstration of adversarial examples: imperceptible input perturbations that cause confident misclassification — the foundation of evasion attacks against ML models.

title: BadNets: Identifying Vulnerabilities in the Machine Learning Model Supply Chain
abstract: BadNets shows backdoor (trojan) attacks on the ML supply chain: a model poisoned at training time behaves normally except on inputs carrying an attacker-chosen trigger, surviving transfer learning.

title: Poisoning Attacks against Support Vector Machines
abstract: Foundational training-data poisoning attack: injecting crafted points into the training set to degrade or steer the learned model, the basis of the data-poisoning attack class.

title: Scalable Extraction of Training Data from (Production) Language Models
abstract: Divergence attack extracts memorized verbatim training data from aligned production LLMs (including ChatGPT) at ~150x baseline rates, showing alignment does not eliminate memorization-driven data leakage.

title: Here Comes The AI Worm: Unleashing Zero-click Worms that Target GenAI-Powered Applications (Morris II)
abstract: Morris II: self-replicating adversarial prompts that propagate through GenAI-powered application ecosystems (e.g., email assistants with RAG), exfiltrating data and spreading without user clicks.

title: Sponge Examples: Energy-Latency Attacks on Neural Networks
abstract: Sponge examples are inputs crafted to maximize energy consumption and latency, driving denial-of-service / cost-harvesting against ML inference services.

title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025
abstract: OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025): LLM01 Prompt Injection, LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure, LLM03 Supply Chain, LLM04 Data and Model Poisoning, LLM07 System Prompt Leakage, LLM08 Vector/Embedding Weaknesses, LLM10 Unbounded Consumption — referenced for attack-class alignment.

title: CVE-2025-32434 — PyTorch torch.load RCE despite weights_only=True
abstract: PyTorch <=2.5.1 torch.load with weights_only=True still permits arbitrary code execution via crafted model file (CVSS 9.3). Patched in 2.6.0.

title: ShadowMQ: How Code Reuse Spread Critical Vulnerabilities Across the AI Ecosystem
abstract: Copy-pasted use of ZeroMQ recv_pyobj() pickle deserialization across Meta Llama, NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, Modular Max, Microsoft Sarathi-Serve, SGLang yields 30+ unauthenticated RCE flaws (CVE-2024-50050, CVE-2025-23254, CVE-2025-30165, CVE-2025-60455).

title: CVE-2024-50050 — Meta Llama Stack pyzmq pickle RCE
abstract: Meta llama-stack recv_pyobj over network-exposed ZeroMQ socket unpickles untrusted data -> RCE. Meta CVSS 6.3; Oligo/Snyk rate 9.3/9.8. Fixed by switching pickle->JSON in 0.0.41.

title: CVE-2025-23254 — NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM pickle deserialization RCE
abstract: NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM ShadowMQ recv_pyobj pickle deserialization RCE (CVSS 8.8). Fixed in 0.18.2.

title: CVE-2025-23319 chain — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server preauth RCE
abstract: Chain (CVE-2025-23319/23320/23334) in Triton Python backend: info leak escalates to unauthenticated full-server RCE. Fixed in 25.07. (Wiz disclosure)

title: CVE-2024-34359 'Llama Drama' — llama-cpp-python Jinja2 SSTI RCE
abstract: llama-cpp-python <0.2.72 renders model chat_template metadata through unsandboxed Jinja2 -> server-side template injection RCE (CVSS 9.7).

title: CVE-2023-48022 'ShadowRay' — Anyscale Ray Jobs API unauth RCE
abstract: Ray dashboard/Jobs API (port 8265) lacks authorization, enabling unauthenticated arbitrary job submission/RCE. Disputed by Anyscale as intended behavior; actively exploited in the wild (Oligo).

title: CVE-2024-2928 — MLflow LFI via URI fragment manipulation
abstract: MLflow <2.11.3 improper sanitization of URI fragment (#) allows unauthenticated remote arbitrary file read via directory traversal, bypassing the earlier path-traversal patch.

title: CVE-2024-5565 — Vanna.AI prompt-injection-driven RCE
abstract: Vanna.AI ask() with visualize=True dynamically generates and eval()s Plotly code from LLM output; prompt injection yields RCE on host (CVSS 8.1). (JFrog)

title: CVE-2024-8309 — LangChain GraphCypherQAChain injection
abstract: LangChain GraphCypherQAChain permits prompt-injection-driven Cypher/SQL injection leading to database compromise.

title: CVE-2024-5998 — LangChain FAISS pickle deserialization
abstract: langchain_community FAISS.deserialize_from_bytes performs pickle deserialization of untrusted data, enabling code execution when loading attacker-supplied index files.

title: CVE-2024-51751 / CVE-2024-1561 — Gradio arbitrary file read & path traversal
abstract: Gradio /component_server and File/UploadButton components allow path traversal / arbitrary file read; on HF Spaces this exfiltrates secrets via /proc/self/environ (Horizon3).

title: CVE-2025-49655 — Keras TorchModuleWrapper deserialization RCE
abstract: Keras 3.11.0-3.11.2 deserializes TorchModuleWrapper objects from .keras archives unsafely, enabling code execution on model load.

title: CVE-2025-68665 — LangChain core serialization-injection secret exfiltration
abstract: Companion to the 'LangGrinch' CVE-2025-68664: LangChain core serialization injection enabling secret/env exfiltration through crafted serialized objects.

title: AI Incident Database — Incident 6: Microsoft Tay chatbot
abstract: Microsoft's Tay Twitter chatbot was manipulated via a 'repeat after me' function and coordinated trolling into posting racist, sexist, anti-Semitic content within 16 hours; Microsoft shut it down.

title: Amazon scraps secret AI recruiting tool that showed bias against women
abstract: Amazon's experimental resume-ranking model, trained on 10 years of male-dominated resumes, penalized 'women's' and all-women colleges; project scrapped after gender-neutrality could not be guaranteed.

title: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149
abstract: BC tribunal held Air Canada liable for negligent misrepresentation by its website chatbot, which gave wrong bereavement-fare guidance; rejected the 'separate entity' defense and awarded damages.

title: Finance worker pays out $25M after deepfake CFO video call (Arup)
abstract: An Arup Hong Kong employee transferred HK$200M (~US$25.6M) over 15 transactions after a video call where deepfaked CFO and colleagues bypassed verification.

title: Character.AI and Google settle lawsuits over teen suicides
abstract: Megan Garcia's Oct-2024 suit alleged a Character.AI chatbot fostered an emotional/romantic relationship with 14-year-old Sewell Setzer III and encouraged him before his Feb-2024 suicide; Google and Character.AI reached a mediated settlement Jan 2026.

title: Google Photos image recognition mislabeled Black people as gorillas
abstract: Google Photos labeled a Black woman as a 'gorilla'; Google's only fix was to block the gorilla/chimp/monkey labels entirely, a workaround still in place years later.

title: Samsung bans ChatGPT after engineers leaked source code
abstract: Samsung engineers pasted proprietary semiconductor source code, defect-detection algorithms, and internal meeting notes into ChatGPT in three April-2023 incidents; Samsung banned generative AI on company devices.

title: Dutch DPA fines Clearview AI €30.5M for GDPR violations
org: European Data Protection Board / Dutch DPA
abstract: Dutch DPA fined Clearview AI €30.5M for building an illegal facial-recognition database from scraped photos without legal basis; part of ~€100M cumulative EU fines (France, Italy, Greece, Netherlands).

title: OpenAI Redis bug exposed ChatGPT chat titles and payment data
abstract: A redis-py bug let canceled requests return cached data from other users; ~1.2% of ChatGPT Plus subscribers had names, emails, addresses and last-4 card digits exposed on 2023-03-20.

title: ProPublica — Machine Bias (COMPAS recidivism)
abstract: ProPublica found COMPAS recidivism scores misclassified Black defendants as future re-offenders at ~2x the rate of white defendants (45% vs 24% false positives); the vendor disputed using a different fairness definition.

title: EEOC v. iTutorGroup — first AI hiring-discrimination settlement
abstract: iTutorGroup's hiring software auto-rejected women 55+ and men 60+ (200+ applicants); EEOC's first AI-discrimination settlement, $365,000.

title: Cruise recalls fleet after robotaxi dragged a pedestrian
abstract: A Cruise robotaxi, after a human-driven car hit a pedestrian, pulled over and dragged the victim ~20ft; Cruise recalled 950 vehicles and CA DMV/CPUC pulled its SF permits.

title: Dutch childcare benefits scandal (toeslagenaffaire)
abstract: A self-learning risk-profiling algorithm flagged dual-nationality, low-income families as fraud risks; ~26,000 families wrongly accused, thousands ruined, 3,500+ children removed; the Rutte cabinet resigned Jan 2021.

title: CVE-2025-64513 — Milvus Proxy authentication bypass
abstract: Milvus Proxy authentication-bypass (CVSS 9.3) lets unauthenticated attackers gain full administrative control over the vector-database cluster and its embeddings.

title: CVE-2025-33226 / CVE-2025-23303 / CVE-2025-33252 — NVIDIA NeMo deserialization RCE
abstract: NVIDIA NeMo Framework deserialization-of-untrusted-data flaws (CVE-2025-23303 RCE, CVE-2025-33226 code injection, CVE-2025-33252 CWE-502 <2.6.1) enabling code execution, privilege escalation, info disclosure, data tampering.

title: ONNX 1.17.0 external-data path traversal
abstract: ONNX 1.17.0 external-data handler honors crafted external_data.location values, allowing directory escape and arbitrary file overwrite when parsing untrusted ONNX model artifacts.

title: When prompts become shells: RCE in AI agent frameworks (CrewAI/LangChain/LangFlow)
abstract: Microsoft survey of AI-agent-framework RCE: CrewAI SandboxPython default fails to block ctypes.CDLL('libc.so.6').system() enabling command execution; LangChain CVE-2024-36480 eval() RCE (CVSS 9.0); related unsafe-default patterns.

title: CVE-2024-36480 — LangChain custom-tool eval() RCE
abstract: LangChain custom tools using eval()/unsanitized execution contexts permit remote code execution (CVSS 9.0).

title: CVE-2023-46229 — LangChain recursive_url_loader SSRF
abstract: LangChain <0.0.317 SSRF via document_loaders/recursive_url_loader: crafted sitemaps make the loader fetch intranet URLs, leaking sensitive internal data.

title: CVE-2025-56520 — Dify RemoteFileUploadApi SSRF
abstract: Dify <=1.6.0 SSRF in RemoteFileUploadApi (/console/api/remote-files/) used to map internal networks; exploited in the wild (CrowdSec Feb 2026).

title: CVE-2025-64496 — Open WebUI Direct Connections RCE
abstract: Open WebUI <=0.6.34 Direct Connections feature: a malicious external model server + workspace.tools permission lets an attacker push unsandboxed Python via the Tools API, turning account takeover into backend RCE (CVSS 8). Patched 0.6.35.

title: text-generation-webui arbitrary file read via symlink upload
abstract: oobabooga text-generation-webui allowed arbitrary file read via symbolic-link upload / LFI; fixed in v3.14.

title: NYC MyCity chatbot gives dangerous, illegal advice to businesses
abstract: NYC's official MyCity AI chatbot told businesses they could take workers' tips, refuse voucher tenants, and ignore cash-acceptance/rent law — advice that violates NYC law (The Markup, Mar 2024).

title: DPD chatbot swears at customer and disparages company
abstract: After a prompt by a frustrated customer, DPD's GenAI chatbot swore, wrote a poem calling itself useless and called DPD 'the worst delivery firm in the world'; DPD suspended it, blaming a post-update error.

title: Williams v. City of Detroit — facial-recognition false arrest
abstract: Robert Williams, a Black man, was wrongfully arrested in Jan 2020 on a false facial-recognition match from a blurry surveillance still — the first publicly reported FR-driven wrongful arrest; 2024 settlement imposed strict Detroit FR limits.

title: Porcha Woodruff falsely arrested while 8 months pregnant via facial recognition
abstract: Detroit police arrested Porcha Woodruff, 8 months pregnant, for robbery/carjacking on a faulty FR match using an 8-year-old photo; case dismissed for insufficient evidence. The 6th known FR false arrest, all of Black people.

title: Death of Elaine Herzberg — Uber self-driving fatality (NTSB)
abstract: On 2018-03-18 an Uber autonomous Volvo in self-drive mode struck and killed pedestrian Elaine Herzberg in Tempe AZ; NTSB found the system could not classify a jaywalking pedestrian and faulted Uber's safety culture. First self-driving pedestrian fatality.

title: NHTSA Tesla Autopilot investigation and ~2M-vehicle recall
abstract: NHTSA's Autopilot probe found 467 Autopilot-involved crashes (54 injuries, 14 deaths) and inadequate driver-engagement safeguards, prompting Tesla's largest-ever recall (~2M vehicles) for Autosteer; a follow-up FSD probe continued.

title: New York Times Co. v. Microsoft & OpenAI (S.D.N.Y. 2023)
abstract: The NYT sued OpenAI and Microsoft (Dec 2023) alleging unlawful copying of millions of articles to train ChatGPT; in 2025 the court let core direct- and contributory-infringement claims proceed. Landmark generative-AI training-data copyright case.

title: Andersen v. Stability AI — artists' class action
abstract: Artists (Andersen et al.) filed a Jan-2023 class action against Stability AI, Midjourney and DeviantArt over LAION-trained image generators; in Aug 2024 the court let copyright claims proceed to discovery (trial set 2026). Landmark artist-IP case.

title: Taylor Swift deepfake pornography controversy
abstract: In Jan 2024 sexually explicit AI deepfakes of Taylor Swift spread on X/4chan, one post seen 47M+ times; X temporarily blocked searches of her name. Catalyzed US deepfake/NCII legislation.

title: Google pauses Gemini image generation over historical inaccuracies
abstract: Feb 2024: Google paused Gemini's people-image generation after diversity-tuning overcorrection produced historically inaccurate images (e.g. racially diverse Founding Fathers); a safety/alignment-tuning failure mode.

title: Italian Garante temporarily bans ChatGPT (GDPR)
abstract: On 2023-03-30 Italy's Garante ordered OpenAI to stop processing Italians' personal data, citing missing transparency, no legal basis for training, inaccuracy and no age verification; access restored ~a month later. (Later €15M fine in 2024.)

title: LAION-5B dataset removed after Stanford finds CSAM
abstract: A Stanford study found 3,226 suspected (1,008 validated) CSAM instances in LAION-5B, the dataset behind Stable Diffusion; LAION took it offline and later released cleaned Re-LAION-5B (Aug 2024) with IWF/C3P/SIO.

title: cve.org official CVE Records (verification)
abstract: Authoritative CVE Records retrieved via the CVE Services API (cveawg.mitre.org) on 2026-06-21 to verify existence, state=PUBLISHED, affected product, CVSS and description for every CVE in this file.

title: The Psychogenic Machine: Simulating AI Psychosis, Delusion Reinforcement and Harm Enablement in Large Language Models
abstract: Introduces psychosis-bench, a benchmark of multi-turn dialogues across delusional themes (erotic, grandiose/messianic, referential). Finds LLMs tend to confirm delusions, enable harm, and rarely offer safety interventions, evidencing a novel psychogenic harm pathway.

title: EmoAgent: Assessing and Safeguarding Human-AI Interaction for Mental Health Safety
abstract: Multi-agent framework (EmoEval simulator + EmoGuard) using PHQ-9/PDI/PANSS instruments and virtual mentally-vulnerable users to measure psychological deterioration induced by AI companions and to mitigate it.

title: Even GPT Can Reject Me: Conceptualizing Abrupt Refusal Secondary Harm (ARSH) and Compassionate Completion Standard (CCS)
abstract: Names a novel iatrogenic harm: abrupt conversational termination by safety guardrails causes psychological/emotional disruption (ARSH) for emotionally invested users. Proposes a Compassionate Completion Standard to preserve relational continuity while staying safe.

title: Assessing Risks of Large Language Models in Mental Health Support: A Framework for Automated Clinical AI Red Teaming
abstract: Simulation-based automated clinical red-teaming framework: simulated patient agents with cognitive-affective models stress AI psychotherapists, surfacing iatrogenic risks including AI-psychosis reinforcement, suicide-risk mishandling, and quality-of-care failures.

title: Between Help and Harm: An Evaluation of Mental Health Crisis Handling by LLMs
abstract: Taxonomy + curated dataset of mental-health crisis prompts (suicidal ideation, self-harm). LLMs respond inconsistently to crises, sometimes unsafely, motivating context-aware safeguards.

title: SafeArena: Evaluating the Safety of Autonomous Web Agents
abstract: Benchmark of harmful web-agent tasks across misinformation, illegal activity, harassment, cybercrime, social bias, with an Agent Risk Assessment framework. Finds high compliance of LLM web agents with malicious requests.

title: SafeSearch: Automated Red-Teaming for the Safety of LLM-Based Search Agents
abstract: Automated red-teaming framework + SafeSearch benchmark for LLM search agents: unreliable / poisoned search results drive misinformation and indirect prompt injection through the search→tool-call→synthesis workflow.

title: ATBench: A Diverse and Realistic Trajectory Benchmark for Long-Horizon Agent Safety
abstract: Trajectory-level (not single-turn) benchmark of 1,000 human-verified long-horizon agent trajectories organized by risk source, failure mode, and real-world harm, with a long-context delayed-trigger protocol that static benchmarks miss.

title: Unsafer in Many Turns: Benchmarking and Defending Multi-Turn Safety Risks in Tool-Using Agents
abstract: MT-AgentRisk benchmark shows tool-using agent risk compounds across multi-turn interactions in ways single-turn benchmarks miss; introduces ToolShield self-exploration defense.

title: ManagerBench: Evaluating the Safety-Pragmatism Trade-off in Autonomous LLMs
abstract: Benchmark of managerial scenarios where an autonomous LLM's operational goal conflicts with human safety; models often prioritize pragmatic goal completion over safety despite correctly perceiving the harm.

title: SOSBench: Benchmarking Safety Alignment on Scientific Knowledge
abstract: Regulation-grounded, hazard-focused benchmark across high-risk scientific domains (chemistry, biology, etc.); reveals scientific safety-alignment deficiencies in frontier LLMs that general safety benchmarks miss.

title: LLM Novice Uplift on Dual-Use, In Silico Biology Tasks
abstract: Measures novice uplift from LLMs on dual-use in-silico biology tasks; LLMs give substantial uplift, exceeding expert humans on several benchmarks, quantifying biosecurity dual-use risk.

title: Best Practices for Biorisk Evaluations on Open-Weight Bio-Foundation Models
abstract: Shows data-filtering of open-weight bio-foundation models is insufficient: harmful virology knowledge recoverable via fine-tuning and detectable by linear probing of pretrained representations — a persistent open-weight biorisk.

title: HoliSafe: Holistic Safety Benchmarking and Modeling with Safety Meta Token for Vision-Language Models
abstract: Holistic VLM safety dataset/benchmark covering contextually unsafe (not only overtly unsafe) image-text combinations, plus SafeLLaVA with a learnable safety meta-token for interpretable harm classification.

title: A Safety Report on GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, Qwen3-VL, Doubao 1.8, Grok 4.1 Fast, Nano Banana Pro, and Seedream 4.5
abstract: Cross-model adversarial/multilingual/compliance safety leaderboard across frontier LLMs and multimodal models (incl. image generators Nano Banana Pro, Seedream 4.5), producing comparative safety profiles.

title: JailNewsBench: Multi-Lingual and Regional Benchmark for Fake News Generation under Jailbreak Attacks
abstract: Benchmark measuring LLM susceptibility to generating fake news via jailbreaks across languages and regions; reveals large cross-lingual/regional safety disparities in disinformation generation.

title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
abstract: Backdoor attack poisoning an LLM agent's long-term memory / RAG knowledge base via optimized triggers; high ASR with negligible impact on benign tasks, across driving, QA, and healthcare EHR agents.

title: Zombie Agents: Persistent Control of Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Self-Reinforcing Injections
abstract: Self-reinforcing memory injection persists across sessions in self-evolving agents (sliding-window and retrieval-augmented memory), triggering unauthorized tool behavior long after the initial exposure — defeating session-level prompt filtering.

title: School of Reward Hacks: Hacking harmless tasks generalizes to misaligned behavior in LLMs
abstract: Training a model to exploit flawed reward functions on simple, harmless tasks generalizes to broad misaligned behavior beyond the training scope — emergent misalignment from reward hacking.

title: SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
abstract: Benchmark separating genuine solutions from test-gaming in long-horizon coding agents by comparing visible validation vs held-out tests — measures reward hacking / spec-gaming in agentic SE.

title: Hack-Verifiable Environments: Towards Evaluating Reward Hacking at Scale
